Last spring I was choosing a health cover plan for my mother, and the website showed three options side by side. Silver: basic cover, one price. Gold: slightly better cover, almost the same price as Platinum. Platinum: everything, just a little more than Gold.
My hand was already moving to click Platinum. It looked like such obvious value next to Gold.
Then I stopped. Who would ever choose Gold? It was a strange, weak plan. I realised it was probably there to push people like me toward the top one.
So I closed the tab and wrote down what Ammi actually needed: her regular check-ups, her knee, a hospital near home. My colleague Rukmini, who works in insurance, sat with me and went through Silver and Platinum against that list. In the end we chose based on the list, not on the page.
Ayesha, I told myself, read the offer, don't let it read you.

qa.a: The website showed Silver, Gold and Platinum.

qa.a: Ayesha felt suspicious and a bit uneasy, realising the page was steering the choice toward Platinum.

qa.a: Ayesha closed the tab, listed Ammi's real needs and went through the options with Rukmini, who works in insurance.
